idiom_name: typed row interfaces over driver rows (pg.Result<T>, prisma.$queryRaw<T>)
implementation_notes: At runtime the TypeScript record set is the same array of plain objects as JavaScript; the type system adds the column contract back. A declared row interface (interface OrderRow { id: number; email: string }) supplied as a generic to the driver (pool.query<OrderRow>(...)) or to an ORM's raw API (prisma.$queryRaw<OrderRow[]>...) replaces the classic RecordSet's metadata; generated clients such as Prisma go further and type findMany() from the schema itself. Because the generic is an assertion and not validation, a schema that must be enforced at runtime needs row parsing (Zod/io-ts) or generated types tied to the database schema.
pitfalls: $queryRaw<T> defaults to unknown and any explicit T is a compile-time assertion: nothing validates the rows at runtime, so a renamed column type-checks and fails in production.
JavaScript numbers are doubles: int8/numeric columns typed as number lose precision beyond 2^53, and raw-query values are not normalised across providers (MySQL booleans arrive as 0/1).
Optional versus nullable: a column missing from the result and a column holding NULL both surface as undefined unless the interface models null explicitly.
